{ "url": "https://core.telegram.org/bots/widgets", "title": "Telegram Widgets", "family": "bot-api", "sha": "dfc14652a3a0a6e5b8405935a78f654abd956e0eb40cafcc33eacf7f2610919c", "checked_at": "2026-11-10T20:52:46.472228+00:00", "changed_at": "2026-11-10T17:50:04.877545+00:00", "error": null, "freshness": { "stale": false, "age_seconds": 342, "max_age_seconds": 21600, "refresh_error": null }, "body": "# Telegram Widgets Bots can send **widgets**: small interactive blocks drawn right inside a message. A widget is one self-contained HTML document with inline CSS and JavaScript, at most 32 KB of HTML and 4 KB after compression. Telegram apps run it on the user's device in a sandbox with **no network access at all**, draw it in the style of the chat, and keep it running while it is on screen: a poll whose bars move as people vote, a price ticker, a board game for two in a group, a promo code that copies on a tap. A widget is **fixed code plus changeable state**. The code, its HTML, is set when the widget is sent and never changes. What changes is the widget's state, and only the bot writes it: the **chat state**, tied to one message and seen only in that chat, and the **shared state**, seen wherever the widget is shown. The widget reads its state and redraws when it changes. It cannot change the state itself, but it can ask the bot with small requests, the way a callback button does. Widgets live in the private chat with the bot, in groups, in messages sent via the bot in inline mode, and in forwards to any chat. Currently, in the production environment, widgets work only in the private chat with the bot. The rest works on the [test server](https://core.telegram.org/bots/widgets#availability). A widget can also be a **shared widget**: one widget on the server, like a poll, that any number of messages show, with one shared state for all of them. This page is a guide to designing and implementing widgets, followed by the reference of the widget's JavaScript object `TelegramWidget`. item.text: В актуальном Bot API есть метод `sendWidget`: он отправляет HTML с JavaScript прямо в личный чат. Для этого счётчика достаточно одного запроса; нажатия будут обрабатываться внутри виджета, а значение — сохраняться на устройстве пользователя.
